# 1 Enoch Chapter 85 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 85 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 85:3 — 'a bull came forth from the earth' — Adam as a bull

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-bull-came-forth-from-the-earth, and-that-bull-was-white" | Literal; no annotation needed for pure translation |
| LOGOS | "a bull came forth from the earth, and that bull was white" | Same; symbolism noted in footnote |
| PNEUMA | Narrative translation with inline notation | Adds [Adam] and [Eve] in brackets within the text |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS clean text with symbolism in the SOPHIA notes section. PNEUMA's inline annotations interrupt the flow and are better placed in the notes. The reader of the SOPHIA text has access to the full symbolism key in the notes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Symbolism in notes, not inline.

---

## 85:4 — 'gored' vs. 'attacked' vs. 'struck'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "gored" | Literal; the action of a bull using its horns |
| LOGOS | "gored" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "attacked" | More general; loses the specific bovine imagery |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'gored' (EMET/LOGOS). The Animal Apocalypse is a sustained animal metaphor; using the specific verb 'gored' (the action of a bull's horns) reinforces the animal framework. 'Attacked' (PNEUMA) loses this precision.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 85:6 — 'lamented with a great lamentation'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lamented-with-a-great-lamentation" | Literal Hebrew/Ge'ez cognate figure (lamented a lamentation) |
| LOGOS | "lamented with a great lamentation" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "mourned for him with tremendous grief" | Paraphrase that loses the cognate figure |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS 'lamented with a great lamentation.' This cognate accusative figure (lamenting a lamentation) is a Semitic literary device that intensifies the grief. Eve's mourning for Abel is made maximally emphatic in the source; this should be preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Cognate figure preserved.

---
